Here's what the field has converged on for your exact use case:

## The pattern everyone is moving to

**Reference-first, never invent-first.** Stop asking AI to invent a look. Curate references, extract them into a committed spec file, then make the AI's job to execute the diff. The canonical loop:

1. **Collect 4–8 reference screenshots** in `/references` (or pull on-demand via MCP — see below).
2. **Extract** into a `DESIGN.md` (Google Stitch format is the de-facto standard) + `tokens.css` with OKLCH colors.
3. **Build first pass** against those tokens.
4. **Playwright MCP screenshots the result**, Claude diffs its own output vs the reference, fixes the deltas.
5. **Commit the spec** — future sessions can't drift.

## The tools you're missing that would actually change your workflow

**MCPs to install** (this is where the leverage is, way more than skills):

- **Mobbin MCP** — Claude pulls real app screenshots on-demand from semantic intent ("show me upgrade prompts"). Paid but cited as the biggest unlock of 2026.
- **shadcn MCP** — `npx shadcn@latest mcp init`. Components installed by name, no copy-paste.
- **Figma MCP** (official) — only if you use Figma. Pulls tokens + variables + Code Connect components.
- **Playwright MCP** — closes the loop. Lets Claude *see* what it just rendered. The single most important missing primitive for design work.
- **Brandfetch API** — given a domain, returns logos/colors/fonts. Free tier 100 req/mo. Best way to seed Claude with an *existing* brand.

**File-based context** (this is the "DESIGN.md format" everyone is converging on):

- **awesome-design-md** ([github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md)) — 70+ ready DESIGN.md files for Linear, Stripe, Vercel, Apple, Cursor, Raycast, etc. Drop one in repo root as a starting point. This is probably the single highest-leverage thing for you to look at right now.
- **uxKero/anydesign** — feed it an image/URL/Figma file, get back `design.md` + `design-tokens.json`. Portable across Claude Code, v0, Lovable, Cursor.

**Reference sources** (where to curate from):

- **Mobbin** for app UI patterns, **Land-book / Lapa Ninja / Httpster** for landing pages, **Godly / Awwwards** for craft, **Cosmos.so** for moodboards (the 2026 designer favorite over Pinterest), **Brand New / Brandbook.club** for brand systems.
- **tweakcn.com** for shadcn theme generation in OKLCH.

## What this means for the three skills you installed

- **impeccable** — keep as orchestrator. Strongest praise across the community.
- **emil-design-eng** — keep for motion/polish. Narrow but well-regarded.
- **taste-skill (13 skills)** — prune. There's real overlap with impeccable + emil, and the style packs (minimalist-ui, industrial-brutalist-ui, etc.) will fight each other if both auto-trigger. Keep at most one (e.g. `design-taste-frontend`) and delete the rest. The honest review in the research flagged hard-coded assumptions (RSC + Tailwind v3/4, Inter banned) you'll be fighting.

## What I'd actually do for you, right now

If you want, I can do this in order:

1. **Prune** the skill list down to: `impeccable`, `emil-design-eng`, `design-taste-frontend`, `brandkit`. Delete the other 11.
2. **Install Playwright MCP and shadcn MCP** so Claude can see what it renders and install components by name.
3. **Pull 2–3 DESIGN.md files** from awesome-design-md as templates so you can see what a real spec looks like before authoring your own.
4. **Set up a `/references` folder convention** in your projects so you have a consistent place to drop screenshots.

Want me to go ahead with all four? Or just (1) and (3) first?
